Yanan Wei joined the group on 1 September 2026 as a visiting PhD student from the [School of Life Sciences](https://njunju.nju.edu.cn/EN/7f/76/c7136a163702/page.htm){target="_blank"}, Nanjing University, for a two-year stay funded by the China Scholarship Council (CSC).

Yanan works on biodiversity–ecosystem functioning and stability, with a particular focus on how species loss, functional traits, soil biota, and multitrophic interactions shape ecosystem processes. His current work is based around a long-term species-removal experiment in an alpine meadow on the Tibetan Plateau, looking at the consequences of losing functional groups, dominant species, common species, and rare species.

His project connects closely with several things we care about in the group: response diversity, ecological stability, species interactions, and how field data can be linked with experimental and modelling approaches. We look forward to a great two years — a very warm welcome to Yanan!
